set.hook: Owner-run fish and Provençal table on Cavalaire's Nouveau Port, built around the grand aïoli.
set.why: The house plays the old Provençal ritual straight: salt cod, boiled vegetables and a garlic sauce thick enough to hold a spoon, the dish Provençal villages still serve at their summer feasts. The Golfe de Saint-Tropez tourist listing files it as a fish restaurant with home-made cooking, right on the port, so the boats you watch from the terrace are the same fleet that sells its catch a few hundred metres along the quay.

set.hook: Year-round bar-restaurant on the Rayol corniche, where Dédé Delmonte has served bouillabaisse since 1985.
set.why: The room began as a 1920s bar-tabac for the men building the coast road, and André Delmonte, Dédé, has run it since 1985. Pudlowski went back in September 2025 and found it open every day from early morning, the weekday lunch menu still at EUR 22.50. The windows face the Bay of Rayol and the isles of Levant and Port-Cros, and a jazz quartet played there every Tuesday in summer 2026.

set.hook: Cavalaire's fishermen sell the morning's catch on Quai Marc Pajot from about 10:00, weather allowing.
set.why: A right going back to Colbert's 1652 ordinance lets Mediterranean fishermen sell part of their catch themselves instead of sending it to auction, and Cavalaire's small boats still do it on the quay. The town's own page says the meeting time follows the boats and the weather, from about ten, and that the fishermen hand out recipes with the fish: bream, red mullet, girelles, rockfish for the soup, a langouste on a good day.

set.hook: Cavalaire's year-round Provençal market, every Wednesday morning on Place Jean Moulin, 08:30–13:00.
set.why: Every Wednesday of the year the stalls go up on Place Jean Moulin, a few streets back from the port: olives, tapenade and anchoïade, pissaladière and pan bagnat to eat on the way, honey from the Maures, and the rosé of the Golfe de Saint-Tropez. In winter it is the town's own market, after the summer crowd has gone, and the one morning to stock a galley with Provençal pantry food without driving to Saint-Tropez.

fish.title: Fish by Cavalaire's water
fish.story: Around Cavalaire the fish tables sit where the boats are, and most of them shut with the season. Le Comptoir des Saveurs, on the Nouveau Port, cooks the Provençal canon of aïoli, daube and pissaladière and keeps a March-to-October season. Le Grand Bleu, the restaurant of the Hôtel de la Calanque, has its terrace on the cliff above the Cron cove, and the hotel stays open until 6 November 2026. Further east at Gigaro, Le Refuge, first opened under the pines in 1964, buys from local fishermen and serves lunch and dinner five days a week until 31 October.
fish.where: Le Comptoir des Saveurs, Cavalaire-sur-Mer; Le Grand Bleu, Cavalaire-sur-Mer; Le Refuge, La Croix-Valmer

corniche.title: Along the Corniche des Maures
corniche.story: West of Cavalaire the coast road climbs onto the Corniche des Maures, and its two tables are the ones on this bay that stay open all year. Maurin des Maures in Le Rayol started as a 1920s bar-tabac, and André Delmonte, Dédé, has run it since 1985; his bouillabaisse is ordered the day before, two people minimum. A little further along, the Café des Jardiniers serves lunch only, inside the Domaine du Rayol, the garden Gilles Clément designed for the Conservatoire du littoral. Chef Tom Ortin cooks there every day of the year except Christmas Day, for visitors who have paid to enter the garden.
corniche.where: Maurin des Maures, Le Rayol-Canadel-sur-Mer; Le Café des Jardiniers, Le Rayol-Canadel-sur-Mer

villages.title: Gassin and Ramatuelle tables
villages.story: Up in the hill villages behind the beaches the restaurants keep summer hours. Bello Visto sits on the Barri, Gassin's rampart walk; MICHELIN lists it for its rock octopus casserole and truffle gnocchi, and its 2026 season ran from 24 April to 11 October. Below the village, the Mouret family's La Verdoyante has a terrace that faces the Minuty vines, takes bookings by phone only, and closed on 4 October. In Ramatuelle, La Forge, in the old village forge, has Paolo Amadori from Le Marche making the pasta and bread himself; it opens daily until 1 November.
villages.where: Bello Visto, Gassin; La Verdoyante, Gassin; La Forge, Ramatuelle

street.title: Off the boat, onto the square
street.story: Cavalaire's cheapest good food is bought standing up. On Quai Marc Pajot the fishermen sell their catch from about ten in the morning, whenever the boats are in and the weather allows; they take rockfish for soup, bream, red mullet and now and then a langouste, a direct-sale right that goes back to Colbert's 1652 ordinance. Every Wednesday of the year the Provençal market fills Place Jean Moulin from 08:30 to 13:00 with tapenade, pissaladière and Maures honey. In the evening Ô Petit Bar, on Rue du Port, pours mojitos looking out over the marina; its tourist listing says it opens every day.
street.where: Fishermen's stand, Cavalaire-sur-Mer; Wednesday market, Cavalaire-sur-Mer; Ô Petit Bar, Cavalaire-sur-Mer
